prompt: How many solutions does the system $2x + 3y = 12$ and $4x + 6y = 18$ have?
hint: Compare the coefficients in the two equations. One left side looks like a multiple of the other, so make them match and see.

hints.text: Compare the coefficients in the two equations. One left side looks like a multiple of the other, so make them match and see.
Multiply the first equation by $2$ to get $4x + 6y = 24$. The second equation says the same left side equals $18$. Can both be true?
The same expression cannot equal both $24$ and $18$, so the lines are parallel and there are no solutions, which is choice B.

learningObjective: Recognize an inconsistent system from proportional coefficients with a mismatched constant.
explanation: Multiply the first equation by $2$ so its left side matches the second equation: $4x + 6y = 24$.
The second equation says the same expression $4x + 6y$ equals $18$. No pair of numbers can make it equal both $24$ and $18$.
The two lines have the same slope and different intercepts, so they are parallel and never meet.
The system therefore has no solutions, which is choice B.

alternativeExplanations.title: Contrast with the previous question
steps: These two questions have identical left sides; only the constant differs.
Matching constants means one line drawn twice — infinitely many solutions. Mismatched constants mean two parallel lines — none.
The coefficients decide *whether* the lines are parallel; the constant decides whether they are the same line.
